title: Top up two guest amenity trays to par and leave the rest on the cart
instruction: Top up both blue guest trays so each holds exactly one yellow soap lying flat and one green shampoo bottle standing upright, taking stock from the grey cart tray, and leave the spare stock on the cart tray.
context: Housekeepers restock guest bathrooms to a par level set by the hotel: they count what is already in the room, add only the difference, and keep the rest on the cart, because extras left in rooms are booked as loss and a short tray brings a guest complaint. Done by: hotel room attendants, housekeeping aides.
setup: A dark grey plastic cart tray is fixed to the table in front of the left arm, its centre 24 cm in front of the arm bases and 19 cm left of the midline: inside 24 cm front to back and 15 cm side to side, a 4 mm floor, walls 5 mm thick and 24 mm tall (2 cm above the floor). Two blue plastic guest trays are fixed to the table, each inside 15 cm front to back and 10 cm side to side, a 4 mm floor, walls 5 mm thick and 14 mm tall (1 cm above the floor), their centres 24 cm in front of the arm bases: the left one 35 cm left of the midline (just outside the left arm), the right one 30 cm right of the midline (in front of the right arm). The soap bars are yellow solid boxes, 3.5 cm front to back, 5 cm side to side and 3 cm tall, 30 g each, lying flat; the shampoo bottles are green solid plastic cylinders, 3.5 cm across and 7 cm tall, 80 g each, standing upright. On the cart tray, in one row along its centre line, stand a soap, a shampoo, a soap and a shampoo, their centres 15, 21, 27 and 33 cm in front of the arm bases. The left guest tray holds one soap, its centre 20 cm in front of the arm bases on the tray's centre line; the right guest tray is empty. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: An item counts as in a tray (guest tray or cart tray) when its centre is inside the tray's inner outline (or within 5 mm past it, leaning on a wall) and its bottom is between 5 mm below and 3 mm above the tray's floor; it is upright when a bottle's long axis is at most 15 degrees from vertical (standing on either end), or when a soap lies flat on any of its four long faces: its 3 cm or its 3.5 cm edge at most 15 degrees from vertical, so it stands 3 cm or 3.5 cm tall (a soap stood on a 3.5 x 3 cm end, 5 cm tall, is not upright). 0.25 each for the three items the guest trays lack at the start: the left tray holding exactly one shampoo, upright; the right tray holding exactly one soap, upright; the right tray holding exactly one shampoo, upright. 0.25 more when all three hold and the left tray also holds exactly one soap, upright (both trays at par). All of it: 1.0. The score is 0 if either guest tray holds two or more soaps or two or more shampoos (in any pose), or if any soap or shampoo is not in a guest tray or the cart tray (on the table or floor, on another item, on a wall, or with its bottom more than 3 mm above the surface under it, as when still held). One exception: an item standing upright on the table (its bottom between 5 mm below and 3 mm above the table top) with its centre in the handover zone, 15 to 30 cm in front of the arm bases and within 10 cm of the midline, is in transit and doesn't zero the score while the guest trays lack at least that many of its kind (trays holding no soap, for soaps; trays holding no bottle, for bottles). It earns nothing; an item there beyond that count zeroes the score as above. The trial ends with success once the score is 1.0 and every soap and bottle has moved less than 1 cm/s (and turned less than 0.5 rad/s) for 2.5 s in a row.
reset_notes: Put two soaps and two shampoos back in a row on the cart tray at their marks (soap, shampoo, soap, shampoo from near to far), one soap back in the left guest tray at its mark, and empty the right guest tray; tape outlines in the trays make this quick. Any soap or bottle works in any soap or bottle spot.
fidelity: Approximate: soap bars are rigid boxes and shampoo bottles solid cylinders, so nothing leaks or dents. The cart tray stands in for a housekeeping cart's top shelf and sits on the same table; all trays are fixed (tape them down for real trials). Every object has the same rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). Stock crosses between the arms by being set down on the table between them, as no single arm reaches both the cart and the right tray.
